group: conclusions and the sub-results behind them
description: Applicator keywords produce a conclusion — the requirement the instance violated — and the sub-results that led to it. The wrappers currently print both as equal INVALID lines, which gives a reason the standing of a requirement. These cases pin what each keyword family reports today, per family, so the recovery can be tested rather than inferred from a prefix rule.

cases.name: contains reports the array's failure, and ajv-validate each element's complaint behind it
cases.description: contains requires one satisfying element. The conclusion is the array's failure; a per-element complaint is a sub-result and states no obligation.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: ['ext1', 'ext2'] does not contain items matching the given schema
ajv-validate: INVALID: /0: must be equal to constant
INVALID: /1: must be equal to constant
INVALID: must contain at least 1 valid item(s)

defect.summary: ajv-validate prints an applicator's sub-results as peers of its conclusion; jsonschema-validate prints the conclusion alone, so the two legs report different numbers of lines.
defect.should: Both legs should report the conclusion as the failure and its sub-results subordinate to it, recovered per keyword family rather than by a prefix rule over schema pointers.

cases.name: an empty array satisfies every items and no contains

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: [] does not contain items matching the given schema
ajv-validate: INVALID: must contain at least 1 valid item(s)

cases.name: anyOf reports its conclusion, and ajv-validate one sub-result per branch tried
cases.description: anyOf reports the conclusion plus one sub-result per branch tried.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 'text' is not valid under any of the given schemas
ajv-validate: INVALID: must be number
INVALID: must be boolean
INVALID: must match a schema in anyOf

defect.should: Both legs should report the conclusion as the failure and its sub-results subordinate to it, recovered per keyword family rather than by a prefix rule over schema pointers.

cases.name: oneOf reports every branch that failed
cases.description: oneOf, like anyOf, reports every branch that failed.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 'published' is not valid under any of the given schemas
ajv-validate: INVALID: must be equal to constant
INVALID: must be equal to constant
INVALID: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

defect.should: Both legs should report the conclusion as the failure and its sub-results subordinate to it, recovered per keyword family rather than by a prefix rule over schema pointers.

cases.name: oneOf fails when more than one branch matches, with no failing sub-result behind it
cases.description: oneOf also fails when more than one branch matches — a conclusion with no failing sub-result behind it.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 5 is valid under each of {'minimum': 0}, {'type': 'number'}
ajv-validate: INVALID: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

cases.name: a conditional reports its conclusion under "if" and the failure under "then"
cases.description: A conditional's conclusion and its sub-results sit at different schema locations: the conclusion under "if", the failure under "then".

ajv-validate: INVALID: must have required property 'radius'
INVALID: must match "then" schema

defect.should: Both legs should report the conclusion as the failure and its sub-results subordinate to it, recovered per keyword family rather than by a prefix rule over schema pointers.

cases.name: a conditional reports the else branch's failure the same way
cases.description: Ajv names the branch in params.failingKeyword; the conclusion still sits under "if".

INVALID: must match "else" schema

cases.description: allOf's branches are peers, not sub-results: each failure stands on its own.

cases.name: a not failure has no failing value to describe
cases.description: A not failure is a success that should not have happened, so there is no failing value to describe.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 'text' should not be valid under {'type': 'string'}
ajv-validate: INVALID: must NOT be valid

cases.name: dependentSchemas applies its schema when the member is present
cases.description: dependentSchemas applies a schema when a member is present.

cases.name: propertyNames applies its schema to member names, so the failing value is a name
cases.description: propertyNames applies its schema to each member name, not to the value — so the failing value is a name.

ajv-validate: INVALID: must match pattern "^[a-z]+$"
INVALID: property name must be valid

cases.description: A failure inside a $ref'd definition: whether the nesting survives the boundary is exactly what a prefix rule over schema pointers cannot be trusted about.
